macrostructure.name: Specimen
macrostructure.reason: Per page-structures.md §1, the brief's centre of gravity is an artifact to inspect — a vault record, a grant, a log line — not a claim to read. A skeptical, workflow-literal engineering audience trusts a real specimen over a padlock illustration or a 'bank-grade encryption' claim, so the page shape follows the product rather than the generic security-marketing template.

thesis: A vault is not a lock you trust once — it's a dial you can watch turn. Haven never shows you a secret's value by default, only its shape (owner, scope, expiry) and a ring that reads how much of its life is left. Access is a request that opens the ring; time closes it again on its own. Every section re-enters the same dial device from a different angle: as a reveal control in the hero, as a step-connector in the mechanism section, and as a status ring on every row of the access log.
signature_spatial_move: A partial tick-marked ring — the vault-dial motif — recurs three times: (1) the hero's secret-record card uses it as the Reveal control (a ring that sweeps closed while the masked value cross-fades to plaintext, then reopens on Hide); (2) the mechanism section's three steps are connected by the same ring drawn as a quarter-turn arc instead of a straight line or numbered circles; (3) the audit-log specimen gives every row a small ring glyph indicating active / rotated / revoked. One motif, three jobs — visible shape, hidden value, told three ways.
whitespace_strategy: Gallery-mode airiness (64–112px section gaps) in the marketing bands; the vault-record card and the access-log block collapse to a dense 4/8px internal rhythm — the declared exception argues 'the marketing breathes, the product is exact', not an oversight.
avoided_template: The default SaaS attractor (centered hero, gradient blob, three identical feature cards, four-column footer) and the security-product cliché (a stock padlock/shield hero photo or icon). Rejected in favor of an asymmetric hero built around a real vault-record specimen, a genuine dense access-log instead of a marketing screenshot, and section-to-section layout variation (see section_architecture).

families.display_and_body: system-ui sans stack (no remote fonts permitted, per offline constraint)
families.mono: ui-monospace / SFMono stack — used for secret keys/values, the access-log specimen, and expiry timestamps

type_system.ratio: 1.25 (major third), base 16px body, moderate 600-weight headings (not 800/black) — calmer than a consumer-marketing scale because a credential store should read exact, not loud
type_system.rules: roman display only (no italic headings); tight negative tracking (~-0.02em) on display sizes; open 1.6 leading on body, 1.1 on display; short uppercase labels only, tracked +0.05em, never running text; body never below 16px (14px reserved for chip/metadata micro-labels only)

spacing_system.density_by_zone: airy (mid, 64–112px gaps) for marketing bands; dense (4/8px) inside the vault-record card and the access-log specimen — a declared Axis-3 exception, not an inconsistency

surface_ramp: #1c1810 overlay-on-dark (sticky nav after scroll, CTA band)
color_system.accent: #7a5115 deep brass/gold (~40° hue) — a physical-vault metallic, chosen outside the indigo/violet 270–330° band taste-lint's ai-cliche-gradient flags, and away from the generic security-product blue. Contrast-checked: 6.29:1 on paper, 6.96:1 on white, 6.96:1 reversed (white-on-brass) — all AA+.
color_system.accent_tint: #f1e2bd pale brass wash — background-only (chips, hover fills), never used for text
color_system.status_secondary: #8a3d1e muted rust, used only for a 'rotating soon' status ring/chip, never as a second brand color (6.85:1 on paper)
color_system.text: #201c15 near-black warm ink primary (15.31:1 on paper), #6d6455 muted secondary (5.26:1 on paper, 5.83:1 on white)

ramp: raised (soft brass-tinted shadow, no border — reserved for exactly one element: the hero card's revealed secret-value state)
overlay (near-solid dark tint + hairline, sticky nav only after scroll, and the CTA band)
depth_system.shadow_recipe: background-tinted (warm brass-grey, never pure black), single soft stop, never doubled with a heavy border on the same surface
depth_system.no_glass: no backdrop-blur anywhere; the sticky nav gains a near-solid paper tint + hairline border on scroll, so legibility never depends on blur

motion_system.entrance: sections fade+rise 8px on scroll-into-view via IntersectionObserver, staggered ~50ms per child, ease-out cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), 300–380ms; content is the real final CSS state and only animates if JS runs (never a visibility gate)
motion_system.interactive: hover/focus transitions 150–200ms ease-out on transform/opacity/color only, never width/height; the hero card's Reveal control sweeps the dial ring closed and cross-fades the masked value to plaintext with no layout shift
motion_system.reduced_motion: prefers-reduced-motion collapses all entrance motion to an instant static state; hover/focus transitions shorten to ~80ms but are not removed (still needed for state feedback); the reveal cross-fade becomes an instant swap
motion_system.forbidden: no overshoot/bounce easing, no linear easing, no animated layout properties, no animating-in focus rings

icon_system.policy_note: generation-craft-defaults.md prescribes the official Phosphor package for the runtime; this is a single offline static HTML file with no build step or network access, so no package can be fetched. Deviation: hand-authored inline SVG line icons, 24x24 viewBox, uniform 1.5px stroke, round joins — matching Phosphor Regular's visual weight and grammar without the literal dependency.

imagery_plan.asset_role: atmospheric hero background texture, decorative only
imagery_plan.prompt_intent: macro brushed-brass vault-dial texture with soft directional light and faint circular tick marks; no text, no logo, no literal padlock icon — materiality, not illustration
imagery_plan.placement: confined to the hero's right-column stage, behind the vault-record specimen card, at reduced opacity so it never carries copy or reduces text contrast — all text sits on solid paper/white/ink surfaces, never directly on the image
imagery_plan.essential_copy_rule: no copy or controls are baked into the image; the card and its text are live HTML layered above it

section_architecture.layout_model: sticky minimal bar: wordmark left, 3 links, CTA button right; hairline bottom border only, gains a near-solid paper tint after scroll

section_architecture.role: state the mechanism (a scoped, self-expiring grant) rather than a generic 'keep secrets safe' claim
section_architecture.layout_model: asymmetric 2-column (55/45): headline + lede + dual CTA left; a vault-record specimen card right (masked value, owner, scope, expiry ring, Reveal control) sitting over the brass-dial texture image on a raised stage
section_architecture.composition_anchor: the vault-record card and its dial-ring Reveal control, whose motif recurs in the next two sections
section_architecture.content_dependency: a secrets vault's hero has to show an actual record, not an abstract padlock — the shape follows the product

section_architecture.role: narrative walkthrough of one grant's lifecycle
section_architecture.layout_model: Narrative Workflow — 3-step flow (Request / Grant / Rotate) connected by a quarter-turn dial arc instead of a straight line or numbered circles; each step card a distinct width, not a repeated equal grid
section_architecture.content_dependency: continues the hero specimen's story (what happens to that exact secret); distinct from the hero via a horizontal stepped rhythm instead of the hero's 2-column split

section_architecture.role: prove every read is logged by showing a real log, not a claim
section_architecture.layout_model: Specimen — a single full-width dense access-log block (monospace timestamps, actor, secret name, action, dial-ring status glyph) with tight line-height on a recessed surface
section_architecture.content_dependency: a security-audience trusts a real log line over a claim; genuine product surface, not decorative window chrome

section_architecture.role: state the product's stance without fabricating evidence
section_architecture.layout_model: honest, non-Stat-Led band — three named principles ('Scoped, not standing' / 'Expires by default' / 'Every read is attributable'), each with a short rationale, arranged as an offset 3-column band with varied vertical start to avoid the 'three identical cards' anti-pattern
section_architecture.content_dependency: replaces a fabricated-metrics stat band with honest, sourceable claims about the product's own design, per page-structures.md §3

section_architecture.layout_model: Catalogue — dense equal-weight grid of 8 named integration targets (source control, CI, cloud KMS, chat/on-call, infra-as-code) each with a small hand-authored glyph; explicitly NOT a customer logo wall
section_architecture.content_dependency: a set of like items reads correctly as a catalogue, not a stat

section_architecture.layout_model: one large statement + dual CTA on a dark overlay band, asymmetric left-aligned, echoing the hero's alignment rather than a centered close band

section_architecture.role: minimal wayfinding, deliberately not the four-column 'AI footer' tell
section_architecture.layout_model: single row: wordmark + 4 links + copyright, no social row, no link columns

structural_fingerprint_note: macrostructure=Specimen, 8 sections, focal viewport=hero (asymmetric split, vault-record specimen over brass-dial imagery), reveal=scroll-staggered entrance, nav=minimal-sticky, footer=single-row-minimal. Recorded for future-generation diversification per page-structures.md §2 even though this benchmark workspace has no prior-surface memory to diff against.
self_declared_deviations: Icon set is hand-authored inline SVG rather than the literal Phosphor package (no network/build step available to fetch it) — matches Phosphor Regular's stroke grammar. See icon_system.policy_note.
